review: Simplicity distinguishes explanatory adequacy from counting entities; closing four-route synthesis retains inaccurate concession narrative as Horn claim, not fact. Lataster conditional grants and qualified ontological aside preserved; no Q&A credit or penalty.

cards.words: Horn uses a homicide analogy to argue that removing an agent can complicate explanation, so simplicity concerns explanatory adequacy rather than automatically minimizing the number of entities.
cards.critique: Strongest feature: Horn’s vivid homicide analogy correctly demonstrates that deleting an agent can make an explanation less plausible and distinguishes raw entity counting from the broader explanatory economy relevant to Ockham’s razor. Principal limitation: The analogy establishes a general methodological possibility, not that a sustaining cosmic agent actually simplifies this evidence or explains it better than naturalism, pantheism, or another worldview. Live burden: Horn must supply the missing comparison that connects the example’s lesson to the universe and shows why his proposed agent reduces unexplained structure rather than merely adding agency. Locked score: 81 The move is concise, clear, and directly responsive to an automatic simplicity objection, but its modest evidential reach cannot support Horn’s further claim that one sustaining agent is already the simplest and most plausible cosmic explanation.

cards.words: Horn’s closing combines contingency, finite causation, fine-tuning, and morality into one unlimited, necessary, personal, perfectly good source, presenting the four routes as sufficient support for classical theism.
cards.critique: Strongest feature: Horn clearly synthesizes four distinct routes and explains how necessity, creative agency, unity, and perfect goodness are intended to converge upon the full classical-theist conclusion rather than generic supernaturalism. Principal limitation: The closing adds no new warrant, inherits each route’s disputed premises, and inaccurately portrays Lataster’s conditional grants and retained objections as concessions or failures to respond. Live burden: Horn must represent the negative replies accurately and show why the cumulative case survives their specific challenges and the unresolved comparison with deistic, pantheistic, plural, or differently moral rivals. Locked score: 78 The synthesis is highly relevant and structurally understandable as the affirmative’s motion-level completion attempt, but evidential dependence and a major charity failure substantially constrain its force; references to question-and-answer material provide no additional support here.

cards.words: Lataster clarifies that his supernaturalism and monotheism grants were conditional discussion concessions, then reiterates probabilistic hiddenness, suffering, and unresolved supernatural alternatives to classical theism.
cards.critique: Strongest feature: Lataster directly corrects Horn’s concession narrative, clarifies that he does not accept the conditionally granted propositions, and integrates probabilistic counterevidence with the unresolved requirement to compare classical theism against supernatural rivals. Principal limitation: The closing provides no completed probability analysis, and its conditional suggestion that a successful ontological argument would favor an unrestricted pantheistic concept remains compressed rather than fully defended. Live burden: He must support affirmative claims that particular rivals are superior while preserving the narrower success of withholding classical theism when generic supernatural evidence fails to discriminate among them. Locked score: 83 The move is exceptionally responsive, burden-sensitive, and calibrated because it rejects logical disproof and universal atheistic certainty, although dense terminology and limited execution of the demanded comparisons prevent an even stronger result.
